title: Factory-catalogue fits=yes parts on an unchanged system are backed facts
body:
**A factory-catalogue part listed for this chassis (fits=yes), on a system nothing has changed, is a fact about the car now without looking at it.**

Camden's call, 2026-09-26, from the desktop app, answering `VER.01`: **"a"**, the recommended option, no words attached.

**The rule.** `confirm` stays on a stage B-K row only where a known change touches the system: the carburettor and air cleaner (the Weber conversion, M-001), emissions equipment whose survival the Weber swap left uncertain (air injection, the altitude compensator, vacuum switching and delay valves, the emission control unit and its label), the removed oil metering pump (D-366), or an optional-equipment row whose fitment is still open (the rear wiper/defogger, tied to stage-A row A2). It also stays wherever the row is already gated on something that resolves it another way: the VIN (`K9`), the trim code (`K10`), a catalogue scan too unclear to read (`K11`), the car on stands (`I0`) or the car apart (`01-electrical:S1`) - those rows are untouched here and settle through their own gate. Everywhere else the row is dropped: the part stays in the record with its catalogue detail, `confirm` comes off it, and the Manual shows it as `from the factory catalogue, not yet seen`.

**What changed today.** 38 stage B-K rows had no gate and none of those exceptions - a colour, VIN-serial or casting variant on a system the Weber conversion never touched (A/C, ignition, ordinary electrical, cooling, interior trim, brakes, suspension, wheels, audio, keys): B1, B18-B22, B24-B26, B29-B31, C1, C2, C4, C5, D5, D10, E1, E2, E6, E9, E12, E32, F1, F2, G4, J1, J3-J7, K1, K4, K5, K7, K8. Each is set `state=dropped`. Their parts (PT077, PT228, PT229, PT240, PT255, PT256, PT263, PT268, PT292, PT322, PT324, PT483, PT198-PT199, PT305, PT589, PT035, PT594, PT311, PT655/657/666, PT553/557, PT645, PT885-887, PT898-900, PT916-919, PT962, PT735, PT795, PT813, PT448, PT492, PT497, PT504, PT516, PT525-530, PT029, PT664, PT667, PT774, PT968) keep their catalogue note but lose the leading `confirm`.

**Left open, untouched by this ruling.** The carburettor/air-cleaner/emissions/metering-pump rows (B3-B16 except B1/B2/B17-B22 as listed, B23, B27, B28, B32-B34, B36, B37, K2), the rear-wiper row G1, every row gated on `K9`/`K10`/`K11`/`I0`/`01-electrical:S1`, and the four K-stage mechanism rows (K9, K10, K11, I0) themselves.

**In the data.** 00-verify `work`: the 38 rows above set `state=dropped`. 00-CAR `parts`: their `note` loses the `confirm` prefix. Closes `VER.01`.

title: The factory harness is not checked before it comes out
body:
**The factory harness is not checked before it comes out; a surviving device's terminal labels are confirmed later, when the new leg is pinned to it.**

Camden's call, 2026-09-26, from the desktop app, answering `VER.02`: **"a"**, the recommended option, no words attached.

**The rule.** The 80 stage-W rows (unplug each factory connector, check its terminals' labels and wire colours against the 1982 diagram) are dropped outright: the electrical project takes the whole factory harness out while the car is apart (D-211, D-411), so the wire colours those rows would record go in the bin with it. The 426 researched terminals stay in the record as read from the 1982 diagram, unchecked; nobody unplugs a connector for a harness that is leaving. What survives the rebuild - the devices themselves - gets its terminal labels confirmed anyway when the new leg is pinned to it, in the build rows.

**In the data.** 00-verify `work`: W1-W80 set `state=dropped`. Closes `VER.02`.

title: What the agents gathered is the record of the stock car; Verify keeps only the stop-and-verify rows
also: D-431 and D-432 applied the same two phone answers (both option a) minutes before this decision was written from his fuller words in chat; this one restates them and goes further (every catalogue-backed row and every measure row, the Manual showing the accepted parts), so it supersedes both. Their four 'different part' rows and blocks VER.03-VER.06 stand.
body:
**Decision.** What the agents have gathered about the stock car from the factory catalogue and the 1982 sources IS the record of the car as it stands, known errors accounted for. A fact is not held back until Camden has looked at it: he verifies only what would stop work if it were wrong, before that work; everything else is checked as it comes up, in the project whose row touches the part. Verify keeps only the stop-and-verify rows.

**His words** (chat, 2026-09-26, verbatim): "first there should be far more part data availavle, i dont need to go through every single fact scraped verify everything you can from hwta all the agens have scraped together about the stoch car, that is exactly what i have (when you account for known errors). then decide weither it is work stoping to verify now or to verify as we go along, make note later to verify some in a project where applicable, then verify should only have the things i neeed to stop and verify before anything else"

**Reading.** This rules block `VER.01` as its option (a): a fits=yes catalogue row on a system nothing has changed is backed; 'confirm' is reserved for a system with a known change. It rules block `VER.02` as its option (a): the 80 wiring-check rows are dropped - the diagram's wire colours are data, and the harness they describe is being replaced; each device's terminals are checked when the new leg is pinned to it (01-electrical E20-E23). He also answered both blocks on his phone before this chat; those answers had not reached GitHub when this was written and are superseded by these words when they land.

**Why.** 290 rows asked him to confirm, one by one, facts the catalogue already states about a car nobody has modified in those places - internal engine parts, trim, brackets - plus 80 unpluggings of a harness that is leaving. His time is the scarce resource (CLAUDE.md §3: over-blocking is a failure), and the Manual hid 173 parts and 129 specs meanwhile.

**Consequences in the data.**
- 00-verify work: every open row of his that asks whether a catalogue part is on the car as described, every 'measure or read off the part' row and every wiring-check row is `dropped`, with a note saying what to check and where when the part is in hand. Kept for him: K9 (read the VIN), K10 (read the trim code), R0 and R3 (the research), and the six rows on systems with a known change - the Weber conversion, the emissions and cold-start hardware: B4, B27, B28, B32, B33, I18. Agent rows stay (L1-L15 the 1982 look-ups, K11 the unreadable scans, R1, R2).
- 00-CAR parts: for the parts those dropped rows covered, the word 'confirm' in the note becomes 'check' (a detail to verify when in hand), so the Manual shows them; the six kept parts keep 'confirm'. Specs from 1982 sources: the same rewrite in `note`; `unverified` specs (a non-factory source) and `other-car` figures stay held - the first is where errors live, the second is what the L rows resolve.
- Block `CAR.04` (confirm vs check as words, or a column) stays his: the rewrite here uses the words convention the merge already follows and is reversible into a column if he picks (b).
- Blocks `VER.01` and `VER.02` are deleted by this decision. Plan row 02-APP P29 is done.
